bib.title: Fisherian Inference and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (Chapter 4, Computer Age Statistical Inference)

question: What are Fisher's methods (maximum likelihood, Fisher information, conditional inference, permutation/randomization) and which survive in computer-age practice?
contributions: Reviews MLE, Fisher information and the asymptotic normal result, conditional inference with ancillaries, and permutation/randomization inference.

results.claim: Normal-model MLE for the gfr data is the sample mean and the (divide-by-n) standard deviation.
results.setup: gfr data (Fig 2.1), n=211, iid sample, MLE by maximizing sum of log densities; normal model (4.6)

results.claim: Gamma model with free lower limit has no closed-form MLE; numerical maximization gives (lambda, sigma, gamma); fits better than normal but not satisfactorily.
results.setup: gfr data (Fig 2.1), n=211, iid sample, MLE by maximizing sum of log densities; gamma model (4.7) with shift parameter
results.note: Greek symbols lost in text extraction; order as printed

results.claim: MLE of the maximum coordinate of 6033 gene means is a flagrant overestimate, so MLE plug-in can mislead in high dimensions.
results.setup: prostate data (Fig 3.4), 6033 genes, theta_i-hat = x_i; target T=max_i theta_i

results.claim: Total Fisher information in an iid sample is n*I and the MLE is approximately N(theta, 1/(nI)) in large samples; no nearly unbiased estimator does better (Cramer-Rao).
results.setup: one-parameter family, regularity conditions, large n

results.claim: Normal sampling with known sigma^2: score sum(x_i-mu)/sigma^2, I=1/sigma^2, so mu-hat=xbar ~ N(mu, sigma^2/n).
results.setup: x_i iid N(mu, sigma^2), sigma^2 known

results.claim: Conditional sd of xbar after a coin flip chose n=25 is 1/sqrt(25)=0.2, whereas the unconditional sd averaging over n=25 or 100 is 0.158.
results.setup: x_i iid N(mu,1); n=25 or 100 with prob 1/2; n=25 happened

results.claim: Fisher's conditional test for the ulcer table uses margins (16,29,21,24) and tests only whether the upper-left count y=9 is too large; the difference was not significant.
results.setup: 45 ulcer patients, new vs old surgery, success/failure (Table 4.1: new 9/12, old 7/17)
results.quote: the number y D 9 is too big under the null

results.claim: Cauchy simulation: conditional variance of the MLE tracks the observed information bound 1/I(x) closely, ranging 0.05 to 0.20 against unconditional 1/(nI)=0.10.
results.setup: Cauchy location, theta=0, n=20, 10,000 samples; MLE variance within deciles-style groups of 1/I(x) (percent groups 0-5,5-15,...,95-100)

results.claim: Permutation test on gene 136 (ALL vs AML) gives significance 0.0026 vs normal-theory 0.0025.
results.setup: leukemia data, 47 ALL and 25 AML, B=10,000 permutations of the two-sample t-statistic; 26 exceeded |t| in absolute value
results.quote: 0.0026 against the null hypothesis of no ALL/AML
results.note: Observed t is printed 3.13 in Sec 4.4 text (with 70 df, p=0.0025) but 3.01 in Fig 4.3 caption and next page; leukemia figure cited as Fig 1.4 in text and Fig 1.3 in caption.

results.claim: Normal-theory two-sample t-test p-value for the same gene is 0.0025 (Student-t, 70 df).
MLE bias is O(1/n) while sd is O(1/sqrt n); MSE = variance + bias^2 with bias^2 = O(1/n^2), negligible except for high-dimensional plug-in (James-Stein).

limits: MLE is dangerous for problems with many parameters; plug-in MLE of a derived quantity can be grossly misleading (p.41).
Derivations are heuristic; regularity conditions needed for differentiating under the integral; careful references in endnotes.
Gamma and normal fits to gfr are both called unsatisfactory (p.41).
Permutation example agreement is called 'a little lucky' (p.50); non-randomized data cannot support causal reading (p.50).
'Contains no information' for ancillaries is contentious (p.46); Fisher's logic of inductive inference and fiducial inference are out of favour (p.44, p.51).
practices: Use MLE as method of first choice: automatic, near-efficient, flat-prior posterior mode (p.39).
Use observed Fisher information I(x) = -l''(theta-hat) for the MLE's accuracy, N(theta-hat, 1/I(x)), rather than plug-in 1/(n I(theta-hat)) (p.47).
Condition on ancillary statistics (sample size, covariates, table margins) for more relevant and simpler inference (p.45-46).
Use permutation tests to avoid normal assumptions, and randomize treatment assignment in experiments (p.50).
Use regularized MLE in high-dimensional problems (p.41).
